rule.description: A function that is not part of a data-owner class implements the owner's analytics by operating on the owner's own data site-by-site (typed member chains rooted at an identifier of the owner class), instead of asking the owner class to compute the result.

checks.description: Non-owner functions that re-implement the module graph owner's analytics (reachability, entry-point distance, module areas) by repeatedly operating on the owner's data.
checks.detected_relation: rule function -> ModuleGraph-owned analytics data and derived state
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Feature envy: the function is more interested in the data of the ModuleGraph class than in its own — the graph analytics it computes belong on the class whose data it primarily accesses.

matches.evidence: collect folds ModuleGraph's dependents closure per source module and re-derives per-module blast radius (areas via areaOf, entry-point membership via entryPoints) into its own local sets, duplicating the reach analytics the owner class already provides.

measurement.inline_rederivation: per-module reverse-closure fold into local Set accumulators

matches.evidence: collect re-implements the owner's memoised entry-point distance walk (frontier over entryPoints, edges read from importMap) into a local distance table and labels each query's area from areaOf, duplicating distanceFromEntry and area analytics that belong on ModuleGraph.

measurement.inline_rederivation: local frontier/distance table built by walking the owner's raw import map

matches.evidence: create eagerly copies ModuleGraph's raw edge data (importMap) into a rule-local module-to-area table built with areaOf, and the rule's visitor and collection closures read that copy instead of asking the owner per module.

measurement.inline_rederivation: eager rule-local Map index over the owner's import data, consumed by closure

excluded.reason: The context is the sanctioned primitive façade handed to every rule; it exposes multiple state getters, so it is not an analytics owner under this rule, and its usage sites are not envied-data access.
Functions inside a detected owner class are the owner's own implementation surface and are skipped by the rule; envy is only credited outside the owner.

FragmentGraph is itself an owner-shaped analytics class; the rule reports functions envying it too, but in this case its consumers only make isolated resolve/reachability queries far below the envy thresholds.

excluded.target: __tests__ directories, fixtures, vendor, generated .d.ts and dist files
excluded.reason: Outside production source; excluded from the checker's analysis domain.
